Carlos C. Goller is a Teaching Professor in the Department of Biological Sciences at North Carolina State University. His academic work connects microbiology, genomics, evidence-based teaching, open pedagogy, and student mentoring through research-rich learning environments.

## Professional Summary

Carlos develops learning experiences that help students participate in authentic scientific inquiry while building confidence, communication skills, and a sense of belonging in STEM. His work spans microbiology, biotechnology, genomics, and biology education, with an emphasis on collaborative teaching practice and public-facing educational resources.

Key areas of focus include:

- Microbiology and genomics education
- Discovery-centered and inquiry-driven teaching
- Open educational resources and accessible course design
- Student mentoring, professional growth, and scientific identity development

## Current Appointment

Carlos currently serves as Teaching Professor in the Department of Biological Sciences at North Carolina State University in Raleigh, North Carolina.
